question.problem:
Find the $51.2$th percentile of the random variable $X$ if the probability distribution function of $X$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{x},\, & 0\le x\le 1, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The $100p$th percentile of a random variable $X$ is the number ${x}_{p}$ such that

$$
P(X\le {x}_{p})=p.
$$

In our case, we want to find the $51.2$th percentile, which corresponds to the decimal $p=0.512.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le {x}_{0.512}) & ={\int }_{0}^{{x}_{0.512}}\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={{x}^{\frac{3}{2}}|}_{0}^{{x}_{0.512}} \\  & ={x}_{0.512}^{\frac{3}{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $51.2$th percentile is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{0.512}^{\frac{3}{2}} & =0.512 \\ {x}_{0.512}^{\frac{1}{2}} & =\sqrt[3]{0.512} \\ {x}_{0.512}^{\frac{1}{2}} & =0.8 \\ {x}_{0.512} & =(0.8)^{2} \\ {x}_{0.512} & =0.64.\end{aligned}
$$
